does: Passes a dry, absorbent biscuit or slice through a liquid for a moment only, so that the outside takes up flavour and softens while the centre stays dry enough to hold the dish together.

intro.what: An absorbent biscuit or slice passes through flavouring liquid without becoming saturated.
intro.why: The surface takes up flavour while enough firmness remains to support the assembled dish. Dipping is different from leaving the piece to soak.

how: Pour the liquid into a shallow dish wide enough to take a whole piece, and let it cool if it is hot.
Hold each piece flat and pass it through the liquid in one quick motion, turning it once.
Lift it out at once and lay it straight into the dish, before the next piece goes in.
Work in a steady rhythm, and try one piece first to judge the time.

cues.text: The piece is damp on the surface and still firm when pressed. It does not bend limp.
The biscuit has darkened only at the surface and not all the way through.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the piece in the liquid, so that it turns to mush and falls apart.
mistakes.fix: Pass it through and lift it out at once.

mistakes.mistake: Dipping into a hot liquid, which soaks the biscuit before it can be lifted.

quiz.question: Why lift the biscuit before it becomes soaked throughout?
choices: It needs to soften until it cannot be lifted intact.
It needs enough firmness to hold the dish together.
It should absorb liquid equally through the centre before assembly.
quiz.because: The method aims for a flavoured surface while retaining a supporting centre.

quiz.question: What should happen to hot dipping liquid before use?
choices: Keep it hot to speed absorption.
Rewarm it before dipping each piece.
quiz.because: Hot liquid soaks the absorbent piece too quickly for the intended controlled dip.

quiz.question: What should a dipped piece feel like?
choices: Damp outside but still firm when pressed.
Limp and unable to hold its shape.
Wet through to the centre and bending under its own weight.
quiz.because: Retained firmness distinguishes a controlled dip from saturation.

quiz.question: The biscuit became mush while sitting in the liquid. What should change?
choices: Leave the next biscuit submerged longer.
Pass it through and lift it straight into the dish.
Press the next biscuit firmly into the liquid.
quiz.because: Prompt lifting limits how much liquid the absorbent piece takes up.

variant_of.differs: The piece spends only a moment in the liquid, enough to dampen the outside and leave a dry heart. It is not left to take the liquid up all the way through.
